summary: Module 2 VERIFY: ran Task 1 (team collaboration data model + migration) against an AI coding agent and reviewed the output against acceptance criteria. (1) Acceptance criteria check -- ALL matched, verified independently: teams, team_members, invitations tables exist in pg_tables; TeamMember has UniqueConstraint(team_id, user_id) named uq_team_members_team_user; Invitation.token unique (invitations_token_key); indexes ix_teams_created_by, ix_team_members_team_id, ix_team_members_user_id, ix_invitations_invitee_email present. 76-test suite passes (exit 0); agent's '75' was a miscount. (2) Unspecified decisions the agent made on its own: FK columns have no ondelete clause (no cascade behavior chosen); server_default values written as quoted literals ('member'/'pending'); index names follow ix_<table>_<col> convention; added ix_team_members_team_id despite UniqueConstraint already covering (task required it). All are acceptable and idiomatic for this codebase -- no conflicts with later tasks. (3) Reproducibility test: the prompt pinned types, lengths, nullability, FK targets, table names, and exact acceptance criteria, so re-running would produce substantially identical output -- low ambiguity. (4) Red flags in the prompt: none -- no 'best practices' phrasing, error/edge expectations were explicit (existing tests must stay green), and output was externally testable (run migration, query pg_tables, run pytest). Verdict: decomposition approach (top-down first pass, medium granularity) produced first-pass usable output; one flaw found -- agent misreported test count (75 vs actual 76) and flagged a pre-existing flaky test, both noted for the trust-audit.
evidence: check_constraints.py: uq_team_members_team_user + invitations_token_key + 5 ix_ indexes present
